result.title: Suspected: governed-intake runtime copy lacks the compose module, so evaluateTriageChecklistState with semanticInput fails at runtime
result.body:
<!-- governed-work-unit-key: sha256:8df176dd6902e4303c42123ee65ac05c285f1874af1e9d32badbb401a12ef8f9 -->

**Status: suspected from source reading, not reproduced.**

## Problem
`scripts/sync-governed-intake-contract.ts` copies only `RUNTIME_FILES` into `src/lib/generated/governed-intake/` (and `publish-governed-intake-bundle-dist.ts` mirrors them to dist): `contract.json`, `evaluator.js`, `feature.md`, `feature.yml`, `governed-intake-body.v1.json`, `task.md`, `task.yml`, `triage-evaluator.js`.

`triage-evaluator.js` is the producer's `governed-intake-triage-state.evaluate` (spencer-shadley/.github release rev 22). When its exported `evaluateTriageChecklistState(body, labels, semanticInput)` gets a `semanticInput`, it does `await import("./governed-intake-triage.compose.js")`. That file is not in the runtime copy, and neither are its static imports:
- `governed-intake-policy-binding.js`
- `governed-intake-body.evaluate.js`
- `governed-intake-triage-state.evaluate.js`
- `governed-intake-triage-policy.evaluate.js`
- `governed-intake-task-profile.evaluate.js`
- `governed-intake-triage-state.migrate.js`
- `governed-intake-task-profile.v1.json`
- `governed-intake-triage-policy.v1.json`

`src/lib/governed-intake-triage.ts` re-exports `evaluateTriageChecklistState` from that runtime copy, so any caller that passes semantic evidence would likely get a module-not-found error. The structural path (no `semanticInput`) is unaffected. The files do exist in `src/lib/generated/governed-intake-bundle/`, but that directory is not on the import path.

Root cause: the runtime copy is a hand-picked subset of the release that doesn't follow the release's import graph.

## Fix
Derive the runtime copy from the release's import closure: start from each runtime entry point and follow every static and dynamic relative import. Don't use a hand-maintained list. Fail sync/publish if a runtime module imports a file the copy lacks. Use canonical payload names; see spencer-shadley/.github#33 for the alias removal.

## Acceptance
- A packaged-runtime test runs against the built dist/package layout (not `src` or the bundle dir). It calls `evaluateTriageChecklistState` with a non-empty `semanticInput` and resolves without a module-resolution error.
- Sync/publish fails when the runtime copy is missing any module in its import closure. A negative test covers this.

Related: spencer-shadley/.github#33, spencer-shadley/code#6453.

## Durable fix and acceptance

- A packaged-runtime test runs against the built dist/package layout (not `src` or the bundle dir). It calls `evaluateTriageChecklistState` with a non-empty `semanticInput` and resolves without a module-resolution error.
- Sync/publish fails when the runtime copy is missing any module in its import closure. A negative test covers this.
- Related: spencer-shadley/.github#33, spencer-shadley/code#6453.

Reuse a current scoped named-file `## Verify` fence when present; otherwise the implementation commissioning path derives and persists/backfills the verification contract before dispatch. If safe scoped verification cannot yet be derived, the leaf waits on verification clarification at implementation preflight rather than remaining untriaged. Before triage can complete, apply exactly one execution-substrate label: `cloud-ready` when implementation can run in an authorized provider-hosted environment, or `local-required` when implementation needs a fleet/local machine. Never leave both or neither on a completed triage. Record `ready` or `not-ready`, a short reason, and any separately required local verification/rollout in the existing triage receipt; an unresolved or `unknown` assessment stays untriaged. If one exact host is required, also apply its machine label. Tracking parents do not inherit every child host or substrate requirement.

Execute close, move, substantive rewrite, or another restricted GitHub effect only when the current role is authorized; otherwise hand the adjudicated effect to the authorized executor with a durable receipt. The triage role does not mint implementation plans or commission implementation writers.

<!-- governed-triage-item: confirm-receipt -->
- [x] **Confirm + receipt**: Clear pending/legacy triage labels only after the contract is satisfied, then apply the current `triaged:vN` stamp last when authorized and read it back. In addition, every substantive model-triaged run records additive model provenance using `triaged-by-<model>-<effort>` derived from authoritative execution receipts (never stripped on re-triage or correction). The single idempotent receipt records checklist completion, direction evidence, disposition, priority/effort/tier, actor-permission outcome, and any handoff. Pickup additionally requires fresh direction evidence. Cosmetic removal of `decomp-in-progress` never gates discovery or reuse.
<!-- governed-triage-item: taxonomy -->
- [x] **Taxonomy**: Validate the current DOCTRINE §14 causal taxonomy and, for defects, distinct prevention and detect/self-heal/recover ladders; conserve new actionable findings as durable work.

- [x] **Outcome-shaped acceptance**: Confirm 'Durable fix and acceptance' states binding acceptance criteria (each names a real consumer or the evidence that stands in for one) rather than a prescribed implementation, and that any implementation suggestions live only in 'Relevant details' as explicitly advisory.
